domain: Duration enrichment: provider estimates, alias rescue, job queue and human reviews
note: HLTB-only user decision supersedes mixed-provider preservation. IGDB estimates/import manifests are discarded, not archived. Provider-neutral authored aliases and human reviews remain. The unattributed legacy duration queue is retired in full and does not fence HLTB work.

game_duration_estimates.role: Per-provider duration estimates with match status, confidence and a jsonb evidence document. The reconcile step chooses between these and writes the winner onto catalog_games.
game_duration_estimates.summary: Retain HLTB evidence/provenance; explicitly discard IGDB rows and provider-only payloads. Source-minus-loaded counts report the authorized disposal.

steam_app_id.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Resolves through migration.game_map to catalog.games.id. Half of the natural (game, provider) key. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
steam_app_id.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

provider.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Which duration provider produced the estimate. Coordinator ruling requires provider to be preserved as a SEPARATE fact from confidence, so it cannot be folded away. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
provider.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

provider_game_id.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: bigint. The provider's own identifier for the matched game - the key that makes an estimate re-checkable, and the anchor for the known HowLongToBeat AppID-identity mismatch on re-released SKUs, where rescue is by exact normalised title or alias rather than by AppID. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
provider_game_id.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

main_story_minutes.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Already EXACT MINUTES; no unit conversion at any point. Would map to a per-provider estimate column, not to catalog.game_features, which holds only the reconciled winner. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
main_story_minutes.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

main_extra_minutes.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: The middle HowLongToBeat tier. Note the singular 'extra' here versus 'main_extras_minutes' on catalog_games - the two spellings are the same tier and a transform must not treat them as different columns. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
main_extra_minutes.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

completionist_minutes.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Exact minutes for full completion. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
completionist_minutes.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

submission_count.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: How many provider submissions the estimate aggregates. This is the SAMPLE SIZE and is the only honest basis for the ordinal confidence; discarding it while keeping a confidence label would leave the label unjustifiable. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
submission_count.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

match_status.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Whether and how the provider row was matched to the Steam app. Distinguishes a confident match from a title-similarity rescue, which is exactly the distinction the profile_steam AppID mismatch makes necessary. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
match_status.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

match_confidence.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Text ordinal over none|low|medium|high. Same class as readiness 4.5: no defensible numeric image, and inventing one fabricates precision. Preserve as an ordinal label. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
match_confidence.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

provider_updated_at.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: When the PROVIDER last updated the estimate, distinct from checked_at, which is when we looked. Both are needed to decide whether a refresh is due. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
provider_updated_at.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

checked_at.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: When we last fetched from the provider. NOT NULL in the source. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
checked_at.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

next_refresh_at.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Provider refresh schedule preserved in the applied catalog.duration_estimates destination. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
next_refresh_at.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

last_error_code.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Why the last fetch failed, as a code rather than free text. Earned history: a persistent provider failure should not be forgotten at cutover. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
last_error_code.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

created_at.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: When the estimate row was first created. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
created_at.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

updated_at.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: Row mutation clock; ordinarily a derived-retirement, but unresolved while the relation has no home. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
updated_at.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

evidence.note: For retained non-IGDB rows: jsonb, NOT NULL. The raw provider response that justifies the estimate. Must be treated as OPAQUE TEXT and hashed as text, never re-serialised (readiness 8.5). Before export it must be checked for anything credential-shaped, since it holds provider responses. IGDB rows are discarded under the HLTB-only user decision.
evidence.transform: Apply the HLTB-only row disposition before the existing typed mapping; exact retained values stay unchanged.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-1 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires duration estimates and provider retry state, and plan 14.2 requires provider evidence and resolver parity. catalog.duration_estimates exists in the M3 migration with a unique (steam_app_id, provider), which is the key this decision asked for.

D-DUR-2 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires ordinal confidence WITHOUT fabricated probabilities. catalog.duration_estimates.match_confidence is a text ordinal constrained to none|low|medium|high, so no numeric image is invented.

game_duration_aliases.role: Operator-authored title aliases that rescue a duration match when AppID identity fails.
game_duration_aliases.summary: Hand-authored provider search aliases are preserved in catalog.duration_aliases as operator decisions a provider refresh must never overwrite.
evidence: coordinator ruling: preserve MANUAL DURATION DECISIONS

steam_app_id.note: Resolves through migration.game_map. The app the alias rescues.
steam_app_id.transform: legacy steam appid -> catalog.games.id through migration.game_map. The alias exists precisely to rescue an app whose identity did not match, so the raw appid is the key and game_id may be NULL.

search_title.note: The exact title to search the provider for. Hand-authored; the entire value of the row. Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped.

release_year.note: Disambiguates remakes and re-releases sharing a title. An integer YEAR, not a date: it must never be widened into a date or timestamp.

review_status.note: Whether the alias has been reviewed and accepted. An operator DECISION.

notes.note: Operator notes explaining why the alias exists. Empty may normalise to null; nonempty must not be truncated or dropped.

updated_at.note: When it was last edited; for a hand-authored row this is a meaningful edit history, not mere row bookkeeping.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-3 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires aliases and manual duration decisions to be preserved, and plan 14.2 lists aliases explicitly. catalog.duration_aliases is a dedicated relation in the M3 migration, which is the second of the two options this decision offered.

game_duration_jobs.role: Work queue for duration enrichment, with a lock lease and retry state.
game_duration_jobs.summary: Discard the entire unattributed obsolete duration queue, including failure/backoff state. Rebuild HLTB work from current HLTB evidence; no provider-only payload archive.
evidence: readiness 14 (queue relations are design confirmations, not migration conflicts)

catalog_duration_reviews.role: Human review responses on catalogue durations, optionally attributed to a reviewing user.
catalog_duration_reviews.summary: Operator duration reviews are preserved in catalog.review_decisions with decision_kind 'duration'. A review by a since-deleted account keeps a NULL reviewer rather than being dropped.
evidence: coordinator ruling on manual duration decisions

steam_appid.note: Resolves through migration.game_map. The app reviewed.
steam_appid.transform: legacy steam appid -> catalog.games.id through migration.game_map.

response_text.note: NOT NULL. The review itself. Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped; empty may normalise to null.

response_kind.note: What kind of response it is (correction, confirmation, rejection). The machine-readable half of the decision.

source_url.note: Where the reviewer got their figure. The evidence behind the decision. Checked for embedded credentials before export.

reviewer_user_id.note: Nullable uuid; resolve through migration.account_map to the nullable reviewer_account_id foreign key. A review by a since-deleted account keeps a null reviewer rather than being dropped.
reviewer_user_id.transform: legacy uuid -> integer account id through migration.account_map. The shared catalogue decision intentionally keeps only the nullable account FK; the source reviewer UUID is available during bounded migration staging and is not retained in this shared row, so ON DELETE SET NULL removes account-linked personal identity while preserving the decision itself.

reviewed_at.note: When the review was made; the ordering key when several reviews disagree.

updated_at.note: When the review was last edited. For a hand-authored decision this is meaningful edit history, not mere row bookkeeping.

settled_decisions: D-DUR-4 SETTLED: ruling 2 requires review/manual-decision destinations and plan 14.2 requires review provenance. catalog.review_decisions.reviewer_account_id is a nullable FK with ON DELETE SET NULL. The source reviewer UUID is bounded staging evidence, so the shared decision outlives the reviewer without leaving personal identity in the catalogue row.
